- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp downward spike followed by rebound, it often overcorrects; cap forecast decline at 5% below recent low.  
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast values are below true outcome, model is underestimating; add 0.5–1.5% to next forecast to catch mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and price is falling, model often underestimates further drop; add 0.5–2% buffer to forecast to avoid under-shock.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the period (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 forecasts.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., -0.16 → +0.27), model often misses the pivot; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
